email.body1:
Stewart, saw Wavetronix debuted Fathom Radar and keeps expanding the intersection lineup.

New product lines usually open more in-market accounts than a territory team can cover while reps ramp on the story, and that is where pipeline slips. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Wavetronix off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Stewart, quick follow-up for Wavetronix.

Expanding the product line creates a window where demand outpaces rep capacity in a territory. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to convert that interest, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Wavetronix needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Stewart, last bit of proof for Wavetronix.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Wavetronix's reply rate likely compares to other transportation-tech vendors. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?

Stewart, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a transportation-tech motion? I will tailor it to Wavetronix either way.
